title: GDScript: Fix separated getter/setter return value and parameter conversions

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Fixes #91689

This PR fixes problems and inconsistencies with getters or setters defined by separate functions, on typed properties. The getter side of this is more involved.

To ensure the getter function result is automatically converted to the property type, without affecting the function itself (as it may have other uses), the compiler now generates new wrapper function for each such getter that needs a conversion. The wrapper just calls the assigned function and converts the results before returning it. The analyzer checks for getter functions that need to have their results converted, marks this using the new `VariableNode::use_getter_conversion` field. The compiler then checks this field and only generates wrappers when this is set.

Example script:
```gdscript
var prop_mismatched_getter: int: get = return_float
var prop_validated_getter: int: get = return_int

func return_float():
	return 1.0

func return_int() -> int:
	return 1

func _run() -> void:
	var target: int = prop_mismatched_getter
	target = prop_validated_getter
```

Bytecode (before):
```
Function return_float()
 0: line 5: 	return 1.0
 2: return const(1.0)
 4: == END ==

Function return_int()
 0: line 8: 	return 1
 2: return const(1)
 4: == END ==

Function _run()
 0: line 11: 	var target: int = prop_mismatched_getter
 2: call-ret stack(4) = self.return_float()
 8: assign stack(3) = stack(4)
 11: line 12: 	target = prop_validated_getter
 13: call-ret stack(4) = self.return_int()
 19: assign stack(3) = stack(4)
 22: == END ==
```

Bytecode (after):
```
Function @prop_mismatched_getter_getter()
 0: line 1: var prop_mismatched_getter: int: get = return_float
 2: call-ret stack(4) = self.return_float()
 8: assign typed builtin (int) stack(3) = stack(4)
 12: return stack(3)
 14: == END ==

Function return_float()
 0: line 5: 	return 1.0
 2: return const(1.0)
 4: == END ==

Function return_int()
 0: line 8: 	return 1
 2: return const(1)
 4: == END ==

Function _run()
 0: line 11: 	var target: int = prop_mismatched_getter
 2: call-ret stack(4) = self.@prop_mismatched_getter_getter()
 8: assign stack(3) = stack(4)
 11: line 12: 	target = prop_validated_getter
 13: call-ret stack(4) = self.return_int()
 19: assign stack(3) = stack(4)
 22: == END ==
```

Note that matching typed functions don't get these wrappers (like `return_int` for `prop_validated_getter` from the example), minimizing overhead.

On the setter side, this fixes a inconsistency with converting the passed parameter to the property type at different points depending on how the setter was called.

Example script:
```gdscript
var prop_weak_setter: int:
	set = weak_setter

func weak_setter(value):
	prop_weak_setter = value
	prints(var_to_str(value), var_to_str(prop_weak_setter))

func _run() -> void:
	var t: Variant = 1.0
	prop_weak_setter = t        # 1.0 1
	set("prop_weak_setter", t)  # 1 1
```

The `GDScript::set()` and `GDScript::_set()` methods performed this conversion regardless of whether the property had a setter or not. I just moved that conversion logic to the branch for direct access without a setter.
